title: Rav Kahana son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov

paragraphs: So it is in Nazir 43b, but Hyman considers the clear plain sense to be that Rav Kahana recited a baraita taught in the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman treats the apparent patronymic as a reference to a baraita from the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. His “clear plain sense” expresses his confidence in that interpretation; it does not establish a father-son identity.

The whole Davidson Nazir 43b paragraph fully writes Rav Kahana berabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. The full Rabbi title is spelled out within berabbi. Hyman’s confident “clear plain sense” instead reads the wording as Kahana reciting a baraita of Eliezer ben Yaakov’s school. The apparent patronymic and that interpretation remain distinct, with no new father-son or school membership binding.
